claims.text: Controlled pre-oxidation at 500–600 °C for 1–2 hours in an oxidizing atmosphere will form a continuous Cr-rich oxide scale on FeNiCrCoCu.
The pre-oxidation-induced oxide scale will be nanocrystalline.
An adhesion-promoting pre-treatment will improve the adherence of the Cr-rich oxide scale to the FeNiCrCoCu film.
The adhesion-promoting pre-treatment will allow the oxide scale to remain intact under mechanical loading.
A continuous Cr-rich oxide scale will minimize direct metal-to-metal contact during high-temperature wear.
The Cr-rich oxide scale will slow further oxidation of the coating.
Reduced direct metal-to-metal contact and slower oxidation will reduce wear-related material removal.
The pre-oxidized, adhesion-promoted coating will have a lower wear rate than the untreated as-deposited coating.
The pre-oxidized, adhesion-promoted coating will have a lower friction coefficient than the untreated as-deposited coating.
After wear testing, the treated surface will retain a continuous and adherent Cr-rich oxide layer.
The untreated coating will exhibit greater wear and possible surface degradation than the treated coating.
The proposed protective mechanism is expected to operate between 500 °C and 700 °C.
The proposed protective mechanism is expected to operate under contact pressures of 50–150 MPa.
Contact pressures of 50–150 MPa at 500–700 °C mimic industrial high-temperature wear conditions.
Performance outside the stated temperature and pressure ranges, particularly under extreme cyclic loading or substantially higher temperatures, is uncertain.
The long-term stability and continuous adherence of the oxide scale during extended cyclic high-temperature wear are uncertain.
